memories.author: D04
memories.text: IBS: symptomatic, on mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide SOS. COPD: stable on tiotropium OD, salbutamol SOS, budesonide-formoterol 200/6 BD. CKD: stage 3a, on telmisartan 40 mg OD, dapagliflozin 10 mg OD, furosemide 20 mg OD, sodium bicarbonate 500 mg BD. Plan: continue meds, check HbA1c in 3 months, lipid profile yearly, spirometry, review weight and waist. Due: HbA1c 2025-07-05.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: mebeverine 135 mg BD after food; ispaghula husk 5 g OD with water; loperamide 2 mg SOS after loose stools; tiotropium inhaler 2 puffs OD; salbutamol inhaler 2 puffs SOS; budesonide-formoterol 200/6 inhaler 2 puffs BD; telmisartan 40 mg OD; dapagliflozin 10 mg OD; furosemide 20 mg OD; sodium bicarbonate 500 mg BD.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: CBC: Hb 13.8 g/dL (13-17), WBC 6.2 x10^9/L (4-10), Plt 210 x10^9/L (150-400). Stool routine: no ova, pus cells 0-1/hpf. tTG-IgA: <4 U/mL (negative <7).

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow-up appointment booked for 2025-07-05 at 10:30 AM with Dr Karthik Hegde (D04).

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Penicillin allergy: rash and angioedema after amoxicillin 5 years ago. Avoid beta-lactams.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: IBS: controlled, occasional bloating. COPD: mild exertional dyspnea, spirometry due. CKD: stable, telmisartan 40 mg, dapagliflozin 10 mg. Weight 78 kg, waist 94 cm (>90 cm male cut‑off). Advised reduced carbohydrate dinner, increased walking. Plan: increase telmisartan to 80 mg OD, repeat HbA1c, lipid profile, spirometry. Due: HbA1c 2025-10-05.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: telmisartan increased to 80 mg OD; all other meds unchanged.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: HbA1c 6.8% (4-5.6). Lipid profile: Cholesterol 202 mg/dL (<200), HDL 38 mg/dL (>40), LDL 122 mg/dL (<100), TG 165 mg/dL (<150). Renal panel: Creatinine 1.3 mg/dL (0.6-1.2), eGFR 52 mL/min/1.73m2 (>60), urine ACR 28 mg/g (<30).

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Spirometry: FEV1 2.1 L (70% pred), FVC 2.8 L (80% pred), FEV1/FVC 0.75 (0.75-0.80). Consistent with mild obstructive pattern, post‑bronchodilator improvement <12%.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Over the past week I have had increased shortness of breath on climbing stairs and need to use my salbutamol inhaler 3‑4 times a day. Also my ankles feel a bit swollen.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: COPD: exacerbation likely, increased rescue inhaler use, mild peripheral edema. IBS: no change. CKD: stable. Plan: start oral prednisolone 20 mg OD for 5 days, continue tiotropium, budesonide‑formoterol, consider checking electrolytes. Review in 1 week.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: prednisolone 20 mg OD for 5 days, then stop.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: CBC: Hb 13.5 g/dL, WBC 8.9 x10^9/L (mild neutrophilia), Plt 225 x10^9/L. CRP 12 mg/L (<5). Electrolytes: Na 138 mmol/L, K 4.6 mmol/L.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Refer to Pulmonology for COPD exacerbation and possible need for long‑term oxygen assessment. Include recent spirometry and spirometry trend.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment changed: follow‑up moved from 2025-10-05 to 2025-10-08 at 11:00 AM with Dr Karthik Hegde (D04).

memories.author: D04
memories.text: IBS: well controlled on current regimen. COPD: stable post‑exacerbation, using tiotropium and budesonide‑formoterol, rescue inhaler <2 times/week. CKD: eGFR 55 mL/min/1.73m2, urine ACR 22 mg/g. Weight 77 kg, waist 92 cm. Advised low‑salt diet, continue sodium bicarbonate. Plan: repeat HbA1c, lipid profile, renal panel in 3 months. Due: HbA1c 2026-04-10.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: HbA1c 6.6% (4-5.6). Lipid profile: Cholesterol 190 mg/dL, HDL 40 mg/dL, LDL 115 mg/dL, TG 150 mg/dL. Renal panel: Creatinine 1.25 mg/dL, eGFR 55 mL/min/1.73m2, urine ACR 22 mg/g.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Pulmonology letter: Patient reviewed, inhaler technique good, no hypoxemia at rest (SpO2 94%). Recommended continue current bronchodilators, consider pulmonary rehab. No long‑term oxygen needed. Return to primary care for routine follow‑up.
